title: Sled average acceleration
change: New context (sled), new numbers (5.0 to 15 m/s over 4.0 s), non-integer answer; distractors are final-velocity, sum-of-velocities and no-division errors.

title: Braking truck acceleration
change: Deceleration with a sign convention; new numbers (24 to 6.0 m/s in 9.0 s); distractors target sign reversal, adding speeds and omitting the time division.

title: Ball rebounding from wall
change: Velocity reversal on a collision with a wall requires careful sign handling; new numbers and context; distractors target same-sign treatment, wrong sign and multiplying by time.

title: Cart net force acceleration
change: New object and non-integer mass (4.5 kg, 18 N); same F/m skill with the same four-style distractors but different values.

title: Pushed crate with friction
change: Adds a second (friction) force so net force must be found first; new mass and forces; distractors ignore friction, add it, or skip dividing by mass.

title: Skater mass from net force
change: Solves for mass instead of acceleration, in an ice-skating context with new numbers; same Newton's-second-law arithmetic skill.

title: Hanging lamp third-law partner
change: Changed from a book on a table to a lamp hanging from a chain; the stem asks the same partner-identification skill; distractors keep the same-object-balanced-force error and add different-pair and net-force errors.

title: Kicked ball third-law partner
change: Impact scenario instead of a static support scenario; same third-law pairing skill; distractors are same-object, and two different-interaction forces.

title: Earth-Moon third-law partner
change: Gravitational pair (gravity-only action at a distance, per CED); same partner-identification skill in an astronomical context.

title: Sled friction on slope
change: Converts the seed's qualitative comparison into a quantitative incline calculation with new context (sled on snowy hill, 30°, 20 kg) while testing the same constant-velocity, balanced-forces idea.

title: Box pushed up ramp
change: Reverses the situation (pushing up instead of sliding down) so the student must account for friction on the opposite side of the balance; same constant-velocity balanced-forces skill.

title: Car at constant velocity
change: Level-road car at constant velocity instead of an incline; same balanced-forces idea; distractors target 'motion requires net force' and 'no resistance' beliefs.

title: Crate push work
change: New context (crate on a warehouse floor), new numbers (25 N, 6.0 m); same product-of-force-and-displacement skill; distractors sum, quotient and spurious factor.

title: Angled pull work
change: Adds an angle (60° above horizontal) to the seed's parallel-force case; new context and numbers; distractors target missing cosine, sine/cosine swap and adding.

title: Friction work sign
change: Negative work from an opposing force; new context and numbers; same work-as-force-times-displacement skill; distractors target the sign, quotient and sum errors.

title: Tripled speed kinetic energy
change: Tripled instead of doubled speed; cycling context; distractors linear, multiplication-by-exponent and cubic errors.

title: Halved speed kinetic energy
change: Speed is reduced instead of increased, with explicit values; asks for the factor; same K ∝ v² skill.

title: Car kinetic energy calculation
change: Quantitative version: new KE after a speed increase (10 to 15 m/s); includes the documented ΔK = ½m(Δv)² misconception from the fact pack.

title: Flowerpot potential energy loss
change: New object and values (3.0 kg, 4.0 m) with g stated as 10 m/s² so all arithmetic is exact; same mgΔh skill with omit-g, omit-height and omit-mass distractors.

title: Climber potential energy gain
change: Gain rather than loss, with a person climbing; new numbers; same product-of-three-factors skill.

title: Ramp potential energy loss
change: Adds the ramp-length distractor (path vs. vertical height); same mgΔh skill with new values.

title: Hammer head tightening
change: New scenario (hammer head) testing Newton's first law/inertia instead of the car passenger; completion-style stem, three misconceptions (stored force, weight change, invented force).

title: Passenger pushed back in seat
change: Start from rest instead of braking; opposite direction of apparent push; same inertia explanation with three misconceptions.

title: Vase and pulled tablecloth
change: Another inertia scenario (tablecloth trick); includes the nuance that friction still acts briefly; three misconceptions.

title: Sign of tension's work while lowering a box
change: New context (lowering a box with a rope) and a why-question; constant-speed condition added.

title: Gravity's work on a ball while it falls
change: Reverses the question: work of gravity on the fall after being given the sign on the rise.

title: Distance while a car speeds up uniformly
change: Speeding up from rest instead of braking; new numbers.

title: Distance for a sled slowing but not stopping
change: Speed does not reach zero, so the area is a trapezoid; different object and numbers.

title: Distance during a runner's acceleration
change: Acceleration is given instead of the time, so the time must be found first; speeds up with nonzero start.

title: Stone thrown horizontally from a bridge
change: Thrown from a bridge with different numbers; new distractor errors.

title: Package dropped from a level-flying drone
change: Package released by moving drone instead of ball rolling off ledge; larger numbers.

change: Small-scale table-top situation with new numbers.

change: Opposite-direction motion on a highway; asks Q relative to P.

change: Frame-addition (ground/train/passenger) rather than subtraction; different scenario.

title: Relative velocity seen from the faster boat
change: Observer is the faster object, so the answer's direction differs from either object's motion.

title: Bowling ball striking a pin
change: Bowling collision with explicit mass mismatch (light pin) and acceleration-based distractors.

title: Person pushing on a wall
change: Contact interaction with a wall (person on skateboard) instead of a collision.

change: Action-at-a-distance (gravity) example with Earth and Moon.

change: Spring defined by natural length and stretched length; force on the hand.

change: Different geometry (crest of a hill, inward is downward) with a symbolic equation choice.

title: Bucket swung in a vertical circle
change: Top of a vertical circle with a rope (tension) instead of a track normal force; sign convention reversed from the seed.

title: Center of mass of two blocks
change: New masses and positions on a shelf; all values recomputed.

change: Third angle (30°) with a different distractor set including double application of cosine.
